name: Measles & vaccine-preventable
value: US, Mexico, Bolivia lose elimination (17 Nov)
summary: PAHO confirmed on 17 Nov that the US, Mexico and Bolivia lost measles elimination; CDC confirms six US deaths in 2026
state: PAHO announced on 17 Nov that the United States, Mexico and Bolivia have lost measles elimination status after 12 months or more of continuous transmission (Health Policy Watch). CDC confirmed six measles-related US deaths in 2026, with cases at their highest since 1991 (Star-Advertiser, 12 Nov). Loss of elimination status meets Watch; searches on 22 Nov found no multi-country surge with clearly rising deaths that would cross the Alert line.
for_you: Two doses of MMR vaccine give strong protection. The NHS and UKHSA advise checking vaccination records before travel, especially to the Americas.
rubric_hit: Loss of elimination status in the US, Mexico and Bolivia = Watch

sources.title: Health Policy Watch — Three countries in the Americas lose measles-free status
Honolulu Star-Advertiser — CDC confirms 6 measles-related deaths in 2026

why: Falling vaccination rates are bringing back diseases once eliminated; measles is the canary for the rest.

rubric.alert: Multi-country surge with rising deaths, or polio/diphtheria resurgence in high-income countries.
rubric.watch: Large outbreaks in high-income countries, or loss of elimination status.
rubric.normal: No large outbreaks in high-income countries.
